steps.message: Let's look at line 435.

Yes, `__hash__` uses `self._meta`:
```python
    def __hash__(self) -> int:\n        if self._hash is not None:\n            return self._hash\n        self._hash = hash(\n            (\n                self._color,\n                self._bgcolor,\n                self._attributes,\n                self._set_attributes,\n                self._link,\n                self._meta,\n            )\n        )\n        return self._hash\n```
So if `_meta` changes, the hash should change. In `clear_meta_and_links`, `style._meta` is set to `None`, but `style._hash` is set to `self._hash`. This is incorrect if `self._meta` was not `None`.

So I should change `style._hash = self._hash` to `style._hash = None` in `clear_meta_and_links`.

```python

```

If `self._link` was not `None`, `style._link` is now `None`.
If `self._meta` was not `None`, `style._meta` is now `None`.
In both cases, the hash of the new `style` object should be different from the hash of `self`.
Therefore, `style._hash` should be `None` so that it is recomputed when needed.

Wait, if `self._link` was already `None` and `self._meta` was already `None`, then `self._hash` would be the same as the hash of the new `style` object. But setting it to `None` is safer and will just cause it to be recomputed once.

If I set `style._hash = None`, it will be recomputed on the first call to `__hash__`.

The bug was in the `clear_meta_and_links` method of the `Style` class in `rich/style.py`. When creating a new `Style` object to return, the method was copying the cached hash from the original style object (`style._hash = self._hash`), even though the metadata and link attributes were being cleared. Since the `__hash__` method depends on these attributes, the cached hash became stale and incorrect. I fixed this by setting `style._hash = None`, which ensures that the hash is recomputed the next time it is accessed.
